title: Finance for 100 senior housing development in Kent, UK
summary: Case study of a development loan arranged by Silver Oak Capital for a 100-unit senior (affordable) housing scheme in Kent, UK, with a gross development value (GDV) of GBP 45 million. Borrower: a developer who had owned the site for almost 20 years and spent almost 5 years securing planning, with strong local-council backing. Need: fully fund construction and, at the same time, refinance an existing bridging loan secured on the site. Challenges reported: the borrower did not want to start building with any pre-sales in place, and the lender had to accept the borrower acting as his own builder rather than appointing a design-and-build contractor. Lender: a London-based senior debt fund. Structure: 65% loan-to-GDV, 78% loan-to-cost, margin 7.25% over base rate, 36-month term, interest and fees rolled up, fees of 1% on entry and 2% on exit; drawn in two tranches, the first used to refinance the existing bridging loan. Outcome as stated: the terms were 'positively received by our clients'. Loan amount in GBP, lender name, exact dates and completion status are NOT stated in the search results. Search metadata suggests the page is roughly 1,851 days old (about 5 years, i.e. circa 2021), but another listing shows it as recent, so the date is uncertain.

Core deal terms (GBP 45m GDV, 65% LTGDV, 78% LTC, 7.25% over base, 36 months, London-based senior debt fund, simultaneous build funding + bridge refinance) appear in both results and are backed by a direct page snippet in (b), so they are reliable. Background and challenge details (site owned ~20 years, planning ~5 years, council backing, no pre-sales, self-build vs design-and-build, two tranches, interest AND fees rolled up, 1% in / 2% out fees) come only from the search tool's paraphrased summary in (a) and were not seen as verbatim page text. NOT revealed: loan amount in GBP (65% of GBP 45m would be about GBP 29.25m, but this is a derivation, not stated), lender name, exact dates, whether the scheme completed, on-page H1, meta description, any FAQ or call to action, author or publication date. 'Senior housing' here refers to housing for older people (senior living), not to 'senior' debt, although the loan itself was senior debt.
